Analysis by Richard Cowan 

See 

RCMP Report On The “Drug Situation in Canada – 2004” Contradicts The Prohibitionist Party Line – Again. Mexico Supplies US With At Least 25 Times More Than Canada. Ontario Rivals British Columbia . 

Americans seemed to have tuned out the war in Iraq, but it will probably get their attention again soon when the death among US troops passes 4,000. 

From 2005, see 

Mexico, the Drugwar and the US National Interest: Never Mind Iraq; We Need To Pay Attention to What We Are Doing to Our Southern Neighbor. 

The population of Mexico is one third of ours, so multiply the following numbers by three to understand their impact on our neighbors. 

Last Friday, the police in Juarez, just across the Rio Grande from El Paso, Texas, reported that they have found 33 bodies buried in a shallow grave. The bodies are mostly male and so are believed to be the result of the Drug War. (Of course, hundreds of women have been murdered there for reasons unknown.) 

Last month the Mexican Federal authorities found nine bodies in another location after a “drug” raid. Because of wide-spread corruption in the local police the “Federales” are even more involved than our DEA. 

While it is easy to deplore police corruption, it has been endemic in Mexico for decades because of low pay and a culture that expected them to supplement their income – just like other public officials up to the Presidente. 

Just this year, there have been dozens of prohibition related murders in Juarez and at least 70 in Tijuana, just south of San Diego. Often the victims have been mutilated to intimidate the police and public. Of course, many of the victims may have been the result of “discipline” within the ranks of the traffickers, known for their tough love – but no one really knows. 

And in the famously beautiful city of Guadalajara, seven people were gunned down in a law office last week. Reporters are also regularly targeted if the write about the corruption or the contraband businesses. 

And as the discovery of these bodies in Juarez proves, no one really knows if the “headline number” of 3,000 since the beginning of last year is really anywhere near the total. 

It is all too easy for people to “disappear” in Mexico, but think how Americans would be screaming, if 9,000 of our citizens had been murdered like this and the families of police officials were murdered in their homes. 

Now however, they have little choice, because even their families may be murdered if they resist. The death toll includes 334 police officers and 39 military personnel.

See 

Program Notes for the MarijuanaNews World Report June 16, 2005 Canada Orders Renee Boje to Surrender. Interview. “Reps” Vote Against Protecting Patients. Democracy? Mexican Army In Nuevo Laredo. 

The involvement of the Mexican military is problematic in other ways. Former members of an elite military group are now the “elite” force behind some of the most violent traffickers. They are called Los Zetas. 

Perhaps Washington is beginning to notice – if not understand – the scale of the problem. Yesterday the Washington Post carried an article “Drug Trade Tyranny on The Border Mexican Cartels Maintain Grasp With Weapons, Cash and Savagery ” 

The Post article reported, “Los Zetas have stocked safe houses with antitank weapons, assault rifles, grenades and other heavy weapons, including some that Mexican law enforcement authorities believe once belonged to the U.S. Army…. 

On Feb. 7, soldiers stormed the dusty "El Mezquito" ranch outside Miguel Aleman, west of Reynosa, and found one of the largest illegal arsenals in recent memory: 89 assault rifles, 83,355 rounds of ammunition, and plastic explosives capable of demolishing buildings. Two days later in nearby Nuevo Laredo, soldiers found a weapons cache that included eight military uniforms to be used as disguises.” 

Doesn’t that sound like another war half a world away? Well, the bad news is that it is right next door and it is a part of a much older war based on lies just like the one in so far away. 

When I listen to demagogues like Lou Dobbs rightly complain about our “broken borders” – although only our southern border is really a problem – and then lie to support the Drug War, I have to keep hoping that the American people and the anti-war movement will notice what is really going on. 

See 

Lou Dobbs and the Second Mexican War. Has It Already Begun? Counting the Costs of the Drugwar. 

We can leave Iraq, but we can’t “leave” Mexico. It is on our border and it isn’t going away.
